title: Generalized supported class characterized on the modified blowup
statement:
Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes on which a fixed prime $\ell$ is invertible, with ideal $I$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $E$ be a rank-$r>0$ finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module and $E\twoheadrightarrow I/I^2$ a surjection [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, $n\geq1$, with small-etale categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Define
$$\mathcal A_a=I^a\times_{I^a/I^{a+1}}\operatorname{Sym}^aE,\qquad B_E=\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A_\bullet),\qquad\pi:B_E\to X,$$
using coefficientwise multiplication and relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. Then $\pi$ is projective, is an isomorphism over $U=X-Y$, and $\pi^{-1}Y=P(E)$. The sheaf $\mathcal O_{B_E}(1)$ is invertible and canonically trivial over $U$. If $E=I/I^2$ and $i$ is regular (locally cut out by a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]), $B_E$ is the ordinary blowup $\operatorname{Proj}_X\bigoplus_a I^a$.
Using the Chern classes of [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities] and the pseudo-divisor operator of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus], put $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O_{P(E)}(1))$ and
$$Q_E=-\sum_{a=0}^{r-1}(-1)^a p^*c_a(E)\xi^{r-1-a},\qquad G=G_{\mathcal O_{B_E}(1),1_U}.$$
There is a split distinguished triangle
$$\Lambda_X\longrightarrow R\pi_*\Lambda_{B_E}\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{a=1}^{r-1}i_*\Lambda_Y(-a)[-2a]\xrightarrow{0}\Lambda_X[1].$$
For every closed $C\subset Y$ the resulting pullback $H_C^q(X,\Lambda(t))\to H_{\pi^{-1}C}^q(B_E,\Lambda(t))$ is injective. For support $Y$ there is an exact sequence
$$0\to H_Y^q(X,\Lambda(t))\xrightarrow{\pi^*}H_{P(E)}^q(B_E,\Lambda(t))\to H^q(P(E),\Lambda(t))/p^*H^q(Y,\Lambda(t))\to0.$$
There is a unique class $\gamma_{i,E}\in H_Y^{2r}(X,\Lambda(r))$ whose pullback is $G(Q_E)$. It has restriction $i^*\gamma_{i,E}=(-1)^rc_r(E)$. For any morphism $v:X'\to X$ with $X'$ Noetherian and $Y'=X'\times_XY$, the pulled-back surjection $E'=v_Y^*E\twoheadrightarrow I'/I'^2$ satisfies $v^*\gamma_{i,E}=\gamma_{i',E'}$. For a surjection $E'\twoheadrightarrow E$ of vector bundles on $Y$ with kernel $K$ and constant $\operatorname{rank}E'=r'$, where $\gamma_{i,E'}$ is formed with the composite surjection $E'\twoheadrightarrow E\twoheadrightarrow I/I^2$, one has
$$\gamma_{i,E'}=(-1)^{r'-r}c_{r'-r}(K)\cdot\gamma_{i,E}.$$
Here the action and the supported groups are those of [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus]. The triangle, its maps, $Q_E$ and $G(Q_E)$ are natural for coefficient reduction $\mathbf Z/\ell^N\to\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ with the power-map Tate comparison. Regularity of $i$ is not assumed except in the indicated identification with the ordinary blowup.

source.place: Expose XVI, Definition 2.2.1.1, Propositions 2.2.1.3-2.2.1.5, Proposition 2.2.2.1, Corollary 2.2.2.3, Lemmas 2.2.2.4 and 2.2.2.6, Definitions 2.2.2.5 and 2.2.2.7, Propositions 2.2.3.1-2.2.3.2. Coefficient naturality uses the same triangle and Kummer powers at each level.

proof.text: Regard the two modules on $Y$ in the displayed fiber product as pushed forward to $X$. The conormal pieces and their multiplication are [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra]; the symmetric algebra is [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. Closed pushforward preserves quasi-coherence by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated]. Thus $A_a$ is the kernel of the difference map from $I^a\oplus i_*\operatorname{Sym}^aE$ to $i_*(I^a/I^{a+1})$, and is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. Pairwise multiplication preserves this kernel because both maps to the conormal algebra are algebra maps. The unit gives $A_0=\mathcal O_X$. Locally products of degree-one lifts show that $\operatorname{Sym}^aE\to I^a/I^{a+1}$ is onto. Both projections from $A_a$ are therefore onto, with $\ker(A_a\to\operatorname{Sym}^aE)=I^{a+1}$ via $z\mapsto(z,0)$. Since $A_a\to I^a$ is onto and $I$ kills the symmetric term, $IA_a=I^{a+1}$ inside this kernel. Hence $A_a/IA_a=\operatorname{Sym}^aE$, compatibly with multiplication. On an affine open the kernel $I^{a+1}$ has finitely many generators because the ring is Noetherian; lifting generators of the finite quotient $\operatorname{Sym}^aE$ together with these kernel generators proves $A_a$ finite.

source.place: XVI, Definition 2.2.1.1 and proof of Proposition 2.2.1.3

proof.text: For each $a$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to the finite cokernel of $A_1^{\otimes a}\to A_a$ at every local ring. At a point of $Y$ its residue quotient is generated by products because $A/IA=\operatorname{Sym}E$; off $Y$, $A=\mathcal O_U[T]$ with $T$ in degree one. The cokernel has zero residue quotient everywhere, so it vanishes. Thus $A$ is generated by the finite module $A_1$. The symmetric universal property gives an epimorphism $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}A_1\twoheadrightarrow A$. By [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] this embeds $B_E$ in $P_X(A_1)$, proving projectivity in the projective-bundle convention; [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper] makes $\pi$ proper. Arbitrary relative-Proj base change [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] applied to $A/IA=\operatorname{Sym}E$ gives $\pi^{-1}Y=P(E)$. Applied over $U$, the explicit algebra $\mathcal O_U[T]$ gives $B_E|_U=U$.

Here is the tautological line and its comparison, using the fraction model [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. On $D_+(s)$ for $s\in A_1$, multiplication by the invertible homogeneous element $s$ identifies $(A_s)_0$ with $(A_s)_1$. Its inverse sends $a/s^m$ to $a/s^{m+1}$. Thus $\mathcal O(1)$ is free there with generator $s$; on overlaps $s=(s/t)t$. These charts cover because $A$ is generated by $A_1$, so $\mathcal O(1)$ is invertible. On $U$ the generator is $T=(1,0)\in A_1|_U$, giving the canonical trivialization. A graded surjection between degree-one-generated algebras preserves these local generators and transition fractions, so it pulls this line back isomorphically, including the trivialization. This applies in particular to a surjection of conormal presentations $E'\twoheadrightarrow E$: componentwise the map $A(E')\to A(E)$ is onto, since a lift of a symmetric tensor has the same image in $I^a/I^{a+1}$, and so gives $B_E\hookrightarrow B_{E'}$ by [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality].

If $I$ is locally generated by a regular sequence and $E=I/I^2$, [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] identifies its conormal algebra with the polynomial algebra on that sequence. Degree one identifies the conormal with the free module on the same generators, so the canonical symmetric-to-conormal map is an isomorphism in all degrees. Taking the fiber product along this isomorphism gives $A_a=I^a$ compatibly with multiplication. Taking relative Proj therefore gives the ordinary blowup $\operatorname{Proj}_X\bigoplus_a I^a$. This is the only use of regularity.

Write $B=B_E$, $P=P(E)$ and $p:P\to Y$. Use the two open-closed triangles of [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] for $(X,Y,U)$ and $(B,P,U)$. Derived pushforward is triangulated by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. There is a map from the first triangle to the $R\pi_*$-image of the second, whose middle map is the unit $\Lambda_X\to R\pi_*\Lambda_B$ and whose right map is $i_*\Lambda_Y\to i_*Rp_*\Lambda_P$. Its left map $j_!\Lambda_U\to R\pi_*j'_!\Lambda_U$ is an isomorphism: by proper base change [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] the restriction over $U$ is the identity and the restriction over $Y$ is the cohomology of zero, as $j'_!\Lambda_U$ restricts to zero on $P$. Open-closed recollement detects isomorphisms by these restrictions. Composition [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence] for the two factorizations of $P\to X$ identifies $R\pi_*i'_*\Lambda_P=i_*Rp_*\Lambda_P$. The mapping-cone diagram of the two triangles therefore identifies
$$\operatorname{Cone}(\Lambda_X\to R\pi_*\Lambda_B)\cong i_*\operatorname{Cone}(\Lambda_Y\to Rp_*\Lambda_P).$$
By [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities], $\Lambda_Y\to Rp_*\Lambda_P$ is the first inclusion in the decomposition with basis $1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^{r-1}$; its cone is $\bigoplus_{a=1}^{r-1}\Lambda_Y(-a)[-2a]$.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 2.2.2.2 and proof of Proposition 2.2.2.1

proof.text: Let $e=e_P(\mathcal O_B(1),1_U)$. For $1\leq a<r$ its supported power $e^a\in H_P^{2a}(B,\Lambda(a))$ gives, under [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] and the exact-inverse-image derived adjunction [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction], a map $i_*\Lambda_Y(-a)[-2a]\to R\pi_*\Lambda_B$: first pull classes from $Y$ to $P$, then apply the supported class on $B$. The restriction rule in [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] says that $e$ restricts to $\xi$, so this map restricts on $P$ to the $\xi^a$ summand. Composing their sum with the cone quotient of Step 5 is the identity on each summand, by the projective-bundle basis [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities]. This is a section of that quotient. Consequently its connecting map is zero and the triangle is split, with precisely the asserted maps. For $r=1$ the sum is empty and the unit is an isomorphism. The derived adjunction applies because constant-ring inverse image is exact and left adjoint to direct image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], and small-etale module sheaves have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives].

Apply supported cohomology to the split triangle, after tensoring by $\Lambda(t)$. The supported direct image is identified with $R\Gamma_{\pi^{-1}C}(B,-)$: by [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] it is the fiber of global sections mapping to sections off $C$; composition of derived direct images [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence] computes these same two section complexes on $B$ and on $\pi^{-1}(X-C)$, since restriction to an open commutes with direct image and preserves injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives]. Thus the split inclusion gives injectivity for every closed $C\subset Y$. With $C=Y$, the third term gives $\bigoplus_{a=1}^{r-1}H^{q-2a}(Y,\Lambda(t-a))$. The projective-bundle decomposition [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities] identifies this with $H^q(P,\Lambda(t))/p^*H^q(Y,\Lambda(t))$. The quotient map is restriction to $P$, followed by this quotient, by the cone square in Step 5. This proves the stated short exact sequence, in every bidegree.

source.place: XVI, Corollary 2.2.2.3 and its all-bidegrees remark

proof.text:
The Chern relation [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities] gives
$$\xi Q_E=-\sum_{a=0}^{r-1}(-1)^ap^*c_a(E)\xi^{r-a}=(-1)^rp^*c_r(E).$$
By the restriction rule for $G$ in [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus], the restriction of $G(Q_E)$ to $P$ is this element, so its image in the quotient of Step 7 is zero. Exactness gives a class $\gamma_{i,E}$ pulling back to $G(Q_E)$ and injectivity gives uniqueness. Its restriction to $Y$ satisfies $p^*i^*\gamma_{i,E}=(-1)^rp^*c_r(E)$. The $a=0$ summand of the projective-bundle formula makes $p^*$ injective in every bidegree, proving $i^*\gamma_{i,E}=(-1)^rc_r(E)$. In rank one $Q_E=-1$, so this gives $\pi^*\gamma=-e$, fixing the ideal-normalized sign.

For arbitrary $v:X'\to X$, use [lem-per-conormal-presentation-proj-base-change] to obtain $B_{v_Y^*E}\to X'\times_X B_E\to B_E$, preserving the tautological line, its trivialization, and the map on the projective-bundle closed subschemes. This comparison need not be an isomorphism of schemes. The pullback of $Q_E$ is $Q_{v_Y^*E}$ by the Chern pullback formula [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities], and the supported operator pulls back by [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus]. Hence the pullback of $v^*\gamma_{i,E}$ to the new modified blowup is $G(Q_{v_Y^*E})$. Uniqueness from Step 8 on $X'$ implies $v^*\gamma_{i,E}=\gamma_{i',v_Y^*E}$. No flatness or regularity is used here. Naturality of the supported Kummer class follows from the relative connecting map [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] applied to the exact Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] for the pulled-back trivialized line.

Let $E'\twoheadrightarrow E$ have kernel $K$ of rank $d=r'-r$. Locally the surjection splits by lifting a basis of $E$, so $K$ is locally free of rank $d$. Step 3 supplies $B_E\hookrightarrow B_{E'}$, carrying the tautological line to $\mathcal O_{B_E}(1)$. To compare the two supported classes it suffices to pull to $B_E$, since its pullback from $X$ is injective. Put $k_b=c_b(K)$ and $S_E=\sum_{a=0}^{r-1}(-1)^ac_a(E)\xi^{r-1-a}$, suppressing pullbacks from $Y$. Whitney in [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities] gives $c_j(E')=\sum_{a+b=j}c_a(E)k_b$, where $c_a(E)=0$ for $a>r$ and $k_b=0$ for $b>d$. Expand the finite sum defining $Q_{E'}|_{P(E)}$. For each $b<d$, all terms $a=0,\ldots,r$ occur and their sum is
$$-(-1)^bk_b\xi^{d-1-b}\sum_{a=0}^{r}(-1)^ac_a(E)\xi^{r-a}=0$$
by the projective-bundle relation. For $b=d$, only $a<r$ occurs, leaving $-(-1)^dk_dS_E=(-1)^dk_dQ_E$. This also covers $d=0$ with an empty collection of vanishing terms. Applying $G$ and its projection formula [lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus] gives the equal pullbacks of $\gamma_{i,E'}$ and $(-1)^dc_d(K)\cdot\gamma_{i,E}$. The injection proves their equality on $X$.

For reduction $\Lambda_N\to\Lambda_n$, the Chern classes, projective-bundle basis and products reduce to their counterparts at level $n$ by [lem-per-noetherian-etale-chern-identities, lem-per-noetherian-supported-product-calculus]. The sheaf maps in the open-closed squares of Step 5 are units, counits and restrictions and so commute with the coefficient map. The splitting in Step 6 uses precisely $e^a$, whose reduction is the corresponding power at level $n$. Thus the triangle and all its specified maps are coefficient-natural. The finite sum $Q_E$ reduces term by term and its supported image reduces to $G(Q_E)$. Injectivity at level $n$ also identifies the reduction of $\gamma_{i,E,N}$ with $\gamma_{i,E,n}$. The Tate comparison is the Kummer power map $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{N-n}}$, used by both cited statements; it is not the naive inclusion of roots of unity. For the supported Kummer class, use the natural relative boundary [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] of the exact Kummer sequence [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]: the vertical maps for exponents $\ell^N$ and $\ell^n$ are the power $\ell^{N-n}$ on the kernel and first $\mathbf G_m$, and the identity on the last $\mathbf G_m$. The equality $\ell^n\ell^{N-n}=\ell^N$ makes this a commuting square, proving the asserted reduction of $e$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q03-b75327f36 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and the new node in full against ILO XVI 2.1.1 and 2.2.1.1–2.2.3.2 (pp. 228–234) and checked every cited statement. The statement matches ILO: the sign is positive, since in rank 1 γ = −e(I_D,1) = +c_D; Q_E is ILO's Clf; the coefficients are Z/ℓ^n on small-etale D^+ with the power-map Tate reduction. Steps 1–4 (construction of A and Proj, regular case = blowup): finiteness, A/IA = Sym E, Nakayama generation, the closed immersion into P(A_1) with Stacks 01WC properness, and π⁻¹Y = P(E) by arbitrary Proj base change are all correct. Step 5 is correct: proper base change makes j_! → Rπ_*j'_! an isomorphism, so the two cones agree. Step 6: the powers of e give a section of ρ, so the triangle splits. Step 7: injectivity holds for every closed C ⊂ Y and the exact sequence holds in all bidegrees. Step 8: ξQ_E = (−1)^r c_r(E), and p* is injective. Step 9 uses only the map B' → B, not an isomorphism. Step 10: I re-did the Whitney expansion; the terms with b<d vanish and b=d gives (−1)^d c_d(K) Q_E. Step 11 (Kummer power square) is correct. The new node lem-per-conormal-presentation-proj-base-change (ILO 2.2.1.5) is true, statement-only, and neither restates an item clause nor duplicates an existing node. I tested a case where h is not an isomorphism: X = A¹, I = (x²), X' = Spec k[x]/(x³) gives the nil-immersion Y' → X'. Batch 5: the item's proof adds only the new node to the closure (computed with and without the item's proof_deps). The four flagged cites are generic: def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism is the EGA definition, lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper is Stacks 01WC, lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction is the generic derivedPlus adjunction, and lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring is Stacks 0F0C, reaching sec-poincare-duality only through the generic Stacks 0DV5 node. None is a trace-formula or Poincaré step, so all are accepted. No SGA, no cycle, and the declared tool uses are accepted. Advisory: the statement's 'projective' relies on def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism through stmt_deps only. The older F_ℓ lem-per-generalized-blowup-class is a special case of this Z/ℓ^n item; this is a base-era overlap.
